findings: All fifteen captured views were visually inspected after the final tapered-head and installed-route rebuild.

The tie detail exposes a tapered rounded molded head, real feed opening, integral pawl, thin strap and internal serrations. The full stock view is a flattened inspection pose; the photographed bent tip is not a qualified free-rest shape.

The two sensor coils are separately retained above the U30 exclusion zone, below the guy collar, with their own top and bottom ties. The complete support geometry remains source-preserving under the recorded 30 degree rotation.
The black temperature adapter and separate wind adapter each have two independent ordinary ties. Heights are staggered to avoid the actual RS3 clamp, housing and bracket.
The bottom RS3 view exposes the continuous lead through the bracket hole and two ties securing it along the inclined arm. The actual mesh clearance and enclosure checks complement this visual review.
The hidden-door view exposes two real plugs in distinct logger jacks and the full network leads through separate cable-channel grooves; front views retain both drip loops.
Detail views deliberately clip the observation bounds, exposing open display sections. Those cuts are viewer-only and are not new physical part boundaries.
geometry_limits: Head opening, pawl, serration detail and bent strap shapes are authored inferences; exact manufacturing tolerances and force behavior remain unknown.
The source-specific 300 mm stock length differs from the linked family drawings nominal 305 mm. Both length and bundle discrepancies are retained.
Fourteen source-length ties account for 2.656489798724572 m retained and 1.543510201275428 m cutoffs. The cutoffs and two removed plugs still require physical storage.
Grounding lead, whole-tool and humanoid access, main-scene inventory and source-to-physics material/contact behavior remain incomplete.
No retention, preload, gravity settling, ratchet, electrical, weatherproofing or robot-execution qualification follows from these images.
